topicName: Pub/Sub and Redis Streams (Consumer Groups, ACK, XREADGROUP)
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Pub/Sub versus Redis Streams: Consumer Groups, ACK, and XREADGROUP"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Redis offers multiple ways to handle messaging between applications. While traditional Pub/Sub provides fire-and-forget broadcasting, Redis Streams introduce persistent log-based messaging complete with consumer groups, message acknowledgments, and consumer tracking."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding the Limitations of Pub/Sub"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Redis Pub/Sub is extremely fast and ideal for real-time notifications or chat applications. However, it suffers from a major drawback: it lacks persistence. If a subscriber is offline when a message is published, that message is lost forever. Furthermore, Pub/Sub does not support load balancing messages across multiple workers out of the box; every subscriber receives every message."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Enter Redis Streams"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"Redis Streams solve the persistence and distribution problems by appending messages to an append-only log data structure. Consumers can read historical messages, process them reliably, and track their progress using consumer groups."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a Stream and Adding Messages"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"To add a message to a stream, use the XADD command. Redis automatically generates a unique message ID based on the current timestamp and sequence number."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"XADD mystream * sensor_id 1234 temperature 24.5"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Scaling Workloads with Consumer Groups"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Consumer groups allow a pool of workers to cooperate on consuming a single stream. Messages are distributed among the consumers in the group, ensuring that each message is processed by only one worker. You create a consumer group using XGROUP CREATE."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"XGROUP CREATE mystream mygroup $ MKSTREAM"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"mystream: The target stream to associate with the group."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"mygroup: The name of the newly created consumer group."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"$: Tells Redis to only deliver new messages arriving after the group is created."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"MKSTREAM: Automatically creates the stream if it does not already exist."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Reading Messages with XREADGROUP"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Workers use the XREADGROUP command to read messages assigned specifically to them. This command requires a group name and a consumer name. The special ID '>' tells Redis to deliver only undelivered messages."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"XREADGROUP GROUP mygroup consumer1 COUNT 1 BLOCK 2000 STREAMS mystream >"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"When a consumer reads a message via XREADGROUP, Redis places that message into the consumer group's Pending Entries List (PEL). This tracks messages that have been delivered but not yet acknowledged."},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Acknowledging Messages with XACK"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"To ensure reliable processing, consumers must explicitly acknowledge that they have successfully handled a message using the XACK command. This removes the message from the Pending Entries List."},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"XACK mystream mygroup 1672531200000-0"},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"Handling Failures and Reclaiming Messages"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"If a consumer crashes before running XACK, the message remains in the PEL indefinitely. Redis provides commands like XPENDING to inspect unacknowledged messages and XCLAIM to transfer ownership of abandoned messages to another active consumer, ensuring zero message loss."}]
